why: Whether a write through a MATLAB function that gives a value of another class keeps the object (doc 'Method Invocation'; MATLAB R2026a: `numel`, `size` give a double for an object whose class has no such method) turns on the class's own method set, which a sync moves without touching the calling file: `numel.m` coming into and going from `@Cel/` makes `x = numel(x); sum(x)` in `@Cel/all.m` the class's `sum` (the project rule: the class's own method gives the object back) and back; `Mid`'s superclass list changing from `handle` to `Pak` (which defines `size`) gives `Kid < Mid` an inherited `size`, so `peek(q)` after `q = size(q)` is `Kid::peek`, and back; `size` added to `Kid` itself, and removed. Without the method the write's value is no object of the class, and the call is the plain one. Every step must end where a fresh index ends.

edit.Kid.m:
classdef Kid < Mid
methods
function peek(obj)
end
function obj = size(obj)
end
end
end
